_note: Every sentence on this page is re-run against the UPSTREAM file that produced it, not against this page's own generated data/accountability.json. That is deliberate and it is the same move index/claims.json makes: a page that checks its own derived output only proves the derive script is deterministic, while a page that checks the source proves the sentence is still true. A correction on funding-map/ therefore fails THIS page instead of leaving a flattering number standing here. Paths climb out of accountability/data/ on purpose. The last claim is the staleness guard: it re-runs the derive script's own arithmetic against the shipped accountability.json, so a stale generated file fails loudly rather than rendering yesterday's subtraction.

claims.text: Headline, standfirst and the stat row under the lead figure: of the $106.3 million PIC reports securing, $4,149,515 sits on award lines naming PIC's own organisation, 4.9 percent of the $85,335,784 awarded; the page carries 18 dated commitments; 7 of the 15 rows PIC answers for cannot be filled from any public record.
claims.source: funding-map/data/funding.json recipients[greater-akron-chamber] and meta.totals; timeline/data/timeline.json events where delivered is false; scorecard/data/scorecard.json counts
claims.assert: sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] == 'greater-akron-chamber' for a in r['awards']) == 4149515 and round(sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if r['id'] == 'greater-akron-chamber' for a in r['awards']) / D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'], 3) == 0.049 and len([e for e in D['tl']['events'] if not e['delivered']]) == 18 and D['sc']['counts']['vault'] == 7 and D['sc']['counts']['accountable'] == 15

claims.falsified_if: Any award line naming the Chamber is added, removed or amended. A forward event resolves or is added on the timeline without this page's hero recomputing. A vault row on the internal scorecard becomes publishable. The share is pinned to three digits because the headline prints it, so a $50,000 amendment that moves 4.86 percent to 4.95 percent fails this claim rather than quietly rounding to the same figure.
claims.official_check: USAspending.gov award ED24HDQ0G0413, and the executed state grant agreement SBIG20251005 governance line.

claims.text: Standfirst, the three-way split of the $85,335,784 awarded: $4,149,515 sits on the two lines naming PIC's own organisation, $51,926,305 on lines naming a firm or university doing the work, and the remaining $29,259,964 on lines naming a programme or a building, or on no line at all. claims.actual: (sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if D['rt']['kind'][r['id']] == 'administrator' for a in r['awards']), sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if D['rt']['kind'][r['id']] in set(['firm', 'university']) for a in r['awards']), sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] if D['rt']['kind'][r['id']] == 'program_aggregate' for a in r['awards']), (D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'] - sum(a['amount'] for r in D['fm']['recipients'] for a in r['awards'])), D['fm']['meta']['totals']['awards'])
claims.falsified_if: A recipient is reclassified, added or removed, or an award line is amended, so that the three shares stop summing to the awarded total. The rounded forms are pinned too, so a change large enough to move $51.9 million or $29.3 million by a tenth fails here rather than leaving the standfirst reading a stale split. If the Chamber ever stops being the only administrator-classified recipient, the first share stops meaning PIC's own organisation and this claim fails.
claims.official_check: The executed award lines behind funding-map's recipient list: the seven EDA Tech Hub awards, APEX award ED25OIE0G0108 and the Ohio Innovation Hub grant agreement.
